Cautiously positive and dovish, with incremental support from bank lending dynamics. The FOMC keeps the policy rate at 0–1/4 percent and continues sizable Treasury/MBS purchases and money-market operations to maintain accommodative financial conditions and support credit flow. SLOOS evidence tilts the tone slightly more constructive: large banks eased standards for several residential mortgage categories (GSE-eligible, QM jumbo, and QM non-jumbo/non-GSE), and foreign banks reported strengthened demand for C&I loans. That said, banks still cite concerns about the economic outlook, industry-specific problems, risk tolerance, supervisory/legislative changes, accounting standards, competition, and liquidity—signaling lingering caution, especially for some business segments and small firms. Balancing these mixed but improving credit conditions against persistent risks, the overall tone remains supportive but guarded.
